title: Local food culture highlights
intro: Food spots tied to Singapore's everyday food culture: family-run stalls and long-standing makers behind dishes locals grew up with. We'll keep adding more.

items.name: New Horse Noodles
items.address: 335 Smith St, Chinatown Complex Food Centre #02-148 (Red Zone), Singapore 050335
items.story: Brothers Scott and Troy Lee left finance careers to open this Hakka yong tau foo stall, learning from an 85-year-old hawker in Malacca. Their handmade pieces come with Malaysian-style dark-sauce dry noodles. They have announced a final business day of 25 October 2026.
tips: Reported hours: Sat-Wed, 9:30am-2pm; closed Thu/Fri. The owners advise coming before 1pm. Check with the stall before travelling.
The S$6.50 noodle-and-yong-tau-foo set is the article-reported price, not a live menu quote.
Contains pork; the filling also includes seafood.

items.name: The Neighbourwok
items.address: 177 Bukit Batok West Ave 8, Get Together Coffeeshop, Singapore 650177
items.story: A coffeeshop stall in Bukit Batok known for wet-style Hokkien prawn mee. In the creator's video, a group shares a big plate with large prawns and each gives it an A or A+. The stall's own page lists its address as the Get Together Coffeeshop.
tips: The video is the creator's own taste test, so treat the grades as one group's opinion.
Check opening hours and queues with the stall before you travel.

items.name: Mr & Mrs Mohgan Super Crispy Roti Prata
items.address: 300 Joo Chiat Rd, Tin Yeang Restaurant, Singapore 427551
items.story: A prata couple known for crisp, thin prata with chicken curry, run from a stall inside Tin Yeang Restaurant. Time Out reported in 2019 that the Mohgans had run prata for over thirty years, first down the road at Crane Road.
tips: Listings show morning opening hours and a Wednesday closure. The video title says it sells out by noon, so go early and check before you travel.

video.title: I Finally Try Singapore's LEGENDARY Roti Prata (sold out by noon!)
video.author: Ghib Ojisan

items.name: Kway Guan Huat Joo Chiat Popiah
items.story: Popiah skin made the traditional way, by spreading dough on a hot pan in one smooth motion. The Straits Times reports the shop at 95 Joo Chiat Road was founded in 1938 and is now run by the third generation. The shop describes a family recipe from Fujian and offers popiah tours.
tips: The shophouse was rebuilt in a Peranakan style in 2018, according to the shop.
Check opening hours and tour bookings with the shop before you go.

items.name: Ole Ole Bumbu
items.address: 50A Marine Terrace, Marine Terrace Market & Food Centre #01-307, Singapore 441050
items.story: Eliza and her family run this neighbourhood stall, where warm greetings are part of the daily routine. In OGS's film, she prepares old-school lontong with turnip, jackfruit and dried prawns, and shares how cooking and her regular customers keep her going.
tips: OGS's pinned comment lists 6am to about 2pm, or until sold out. Opening days are not stated; check before travelling.
Dry mee siam appears in the film but is not available every day. Ask what is cooking that morning.
The lontong contains dried prawns. No current menu prices or halal-certification status are confirmed here.

video.title: Why People Travel Across Singapore For This Hawker
video.author: OGS

items.name: Tian Yue Ci Hang Vegetarian Food 天月慈航素食
items.address: 33 Ubi Ave 3, Hoha Eating House, Vertex #01-35, Singapore 408868
items.story: A vegetarian economic-rice (cai fan) stall inside Hoha Eating House in the Ubi industrial estate. Regulars describe a wide selection of freshly cooked dishes made without alliums, with vegan dishes on the regular menu and occasional specials such as lor mee and laksa that appear without a fixed schedule.
tips: Hours: weekday mornings to early afternoon, closed Sat and Sun. Google Maps lists opening at 6am; HappyCow lists 6:30am-1:30pm, and dishes often sell out from about 1:30pm without being replenished. Check before travelling.
Vegetarian stall with vegan dishes - not everything is vegan, so ask. Google shows a $1-10 price band; no current menu prices are verified.

items.name: Terumbu by Orang Laut SG
items.address: 6 Eu Tong Sen St, Chef X, Clarke Quay Central #03-103/104, Singapore 059817
items.story: The first walk-in cafe from Orang Laut SG, the community group that has sold Southern Islander food mostly through weekend deliveries since 2020. Founder Firdaus Sani is a fourth-generation islander whose family was relocated from Pulau Semakau in 1977; at Terumbu ("coral reefs") his mother Noorani Rani cooks family recipes passed down from his grandmother, with a small community gallery on the Southern Islands alongside. The menu is anchored by the Pulau Bowl - asam pedas reef fish, sotong hitam and sambal udang over jasmine rice - and bubur lambuk tenggiri, a mackerel porridge that was an everyday island dish.
tips: Hours: Tue-Sat 11am-9pm, closed Sun and Mon, per the mall's page.
Reported prices: Pulau Bowl S$15.90; bubur lambuk tenggiri S$11.90 with prawns or squid, S$13.90 with both. From CNA and the mall's page, not a live menu quote.
End date differs by source: the mall's page says 22 Dec, CNA says 26 Dec. This card uses the mall's date; confirm before visiting in the final week.
The reef fish served can change with what islander fishermen catch.

note: Illustrations are concept art. The scenes, people and dishes are not photos of these shops or their food.
